instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay till sunset. Gran said this stone would hatch. I taught you to keep a proper observation record; I need your name beside mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun's down. It's still a stone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, write what you saw, not what she hoped. You used to mix those up. Sign and we can call it disproved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign, but she never said which day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're checking the wording at last. Stay while we ring her for a date. Don't leave your old teacher doing this every evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your coat off. This bell-less tower is meant to ring at noon. You timed my experiments for years; I need a witness who knows the routine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twelve-oh-one. We heard nothing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Write silence, not failure; observation before conclusion, remember? Sign it before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then four minutes more. You still rush the finish. I'll fill in our names; you keep watching the time, properly this once.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Apologize to Reality
cards.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your caretaker interview, apologise to the chair. We practised asking permission; you sat without waiting for its answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It can't say yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the apology opening I taught you: 'I'm sorry I mistook your silence for permission.' To the chair, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair. I'll stand for the interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly. Now apologise for making it redundant. I taught you to make amends, not put the injured party out of work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back at my inn, and still knocking after you've arrived. What did I teach you about warning your host? Apologise to the doorway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had to get here to knock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always confuse arrival with preparation. Tell it you're sorry your knuckles didn't give advance notice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, doorway. I did phone ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good initiative, wrong recipient. Now apologise for telling the telephone first. The doorway shouldn't learn about its visitor secondhand.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
cards.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you approve keeping Tuesday's rain in this cup for the wedding? I trained you to plan ahead when you took over the venue; don't stop at booking chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Catch it before it learns to fall. You always waited until a problem knew what it was doing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it leaks onto Wednesday's wedding?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking two bookings ahead. We'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for both dry lawns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approve the museum's invisible landing. I trained you to trust your judgment; it's time your signature did some work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing supporting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've allowed enough confidence for twenty visitors. You used to need a railing before you'd trust a calculation. You're past that now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I certify confidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign under 'load-bearing'. A steady signature, like we practised. Your certainty will hold the inspectors as well; then we can cancel the scaffolding.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's courtyard film, fold the moon while I switch off the lamps. All those paper-folding lessons with me must be worth something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent; there's your crease. You used to ask me where to begin even when I'd marked the line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're ready to work without my hands over yours. I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you take the moon. Can I put your name beside blackout?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're returning yesterday's missing hour before lunch. Put it in this jar. I taught you to collect things without spilling them; take your time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Time doesn't fit in jars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loosen the lid. You always made a small opening and blamed what wouldn't go through it. Try properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm labeling yesterday. Last time you wrote 'tomorrow' on every jar. You're ready for the collecting; leave the dates to me.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
cards.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your old tutor is stumped. Why is the soup staying in that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, don't pretend you know. Change one thing, like we practised: turn the spoon over and watch the soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets which way is down. You finally watched the result instead of your hand. Point it into the sink before we test letting go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. Hold still, like I taught you when we watched birds. What were you thinking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Leaving. But I can't find the exit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, one thought we can test. Think about that bench. No helpful little step this time; you used to spoil the observation that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a clean result. It follows your intentions. Think about the exit again; we'll follow slowly. Even my best pupil doesn't get to run after one successful test.
